title: Gene shows dexterity breakthrough #gene #genesisai #robotichand
description:
Genesis AI unveiled Gene, a robotic hand system that may be the closest yet to human-level dexterity. The Paris-based startup also raised $105 million, with backing that includes former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, as it showcased Gene cooking, making smoothies, solving a Rubik’s Cube mid-air, handling fragile objects, wiring tasks, and even playing piano at human speed.

The core breakthrough is Genesis AI’s sensor glove, which captures human finger motion and touch during real work and transfers that data directly to the robot. Instead of programming tasks one by one, the system learns from demonstrations, creating a faster path to general-purpose manipulation.

That matters because more than 80% of physical labor relies on the human hand, making dexterity one of robotics’ biggest commercial bottlenecks. If Genesis can scale this approach, it could reshape manufacturing, household robotics, skilled labor automation, and the race to capture human manual knowledge before competitors do.
